title: Requirement
description: An external obligation the company is held to: a certification clause, a regulation article, a contractual commitment, or an internally-imposed rule. Requirements state WHAT must be true. Controls state HOW it is made true and verified. A Requirement never names its own controls; the coverage direction is one-way so there is exactly one writer per edge.

framework.description: The obligation's source catalogue. 'contract' covers customer or supplier commitments; 'internal' covers rules the company imposes on itself.

clause.description: The identifier this obligation carries inside its own catalogue (e.g. 'A.8.5', 'CC6.1', 'Art. 32(1)(b)'). Verbatim, so an auditor can find it.

statement.description: What the obligation actually requires, in the company's own words. Not a copy of copyrighted standard text.

owner.description: The accountable party. Accountability for an obligation always rests with a human or a team, never with an agent.

appliesTo.description: Module paths in scope for this obligation. An empty list means company-wide.

status.description: 'out-of-scope' requires a scopeRationale; an unexplained exclusion is an audit finding waiting to happen.

scopeRationale.description: Why this obligation is out of scope or merely planned. Required when status is 'out-of-scope'.

severity.description: Consequence if the obligation is unmet. Drives the coverage gate in the generated control matrix.

externalIds.description: Identifiers this obligation carries in external GRC tooling. Evolutionary mappings; never primary keys.

references.description: Repo-relative paths or URLs supporting the obligation (policy documents, the published standard, the signed contract).
